text: Write the correct structure for a handler whose work takes four seconds. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: //     ___;                             // 1. tell the user immediately, on the loop
//     ___;                             // 2. do the slow work off the loop, post the result back
// The call that gets you back onto the dispatch thread is ___ .
answer: status.setText("Loading...")|new Thread(() -> { String data = fetch(); SwingUtilities.invokeLater(() -> display(data)); }).start()|SwingUtilities.invokeLater
explanation: Three phases and all three are required. The first tells the user something is happening; the second keeps the loop free; the third is not optional, because only the dispatch thread may touch components. Updating components directly from the worker thread is the common mistake, and it will usually work — which is exactly what makes it dangerous.
